newsitem.title: USA: Dole stings Clinton with 'integrity gap' charge.
newsitem.headline: Dole stings Clinton with 'integrity gap' charge.

text.p: Republican challenger Bob Dole threw his hardest punches of the campaign on Tuesday, charging President Bill Clinton and his administration with an "integrity gap ... between their swagger and public scandal."

"No administration has been more self-righteous," Dole said. "But few administrations have been more self-serving. No administration has shown more arrogance. But few have displayed more ethical failures."
The stepped-up attack on White House ethics could be a preview of Wednesday night's crucial final debate with Clinton that Dole must win to move up in the polls exactly three weeks to Election Day.
Many of his advisers have urged Dole to step up his assault on the so-called "character issue" and he showed some signs of agreeing to their argument in the closing days of the campaign.
The Republican candidate spoke a luncheon of the Electronic Industrial Association in the city where he won his party's nomination in August and which will host the last debate.
Dole noted Clinton came into office promising "the most ethical administration in the history of the republic."
But then he ran down a laundry list of what he saw as ethical failures and accused Clinton of avoiding responsibility.

"Among members of this administration there is a growing gap -- an integrity gap -- between the low standards they have adopted and the high honour that they hold," Dole said. "A gap between their swagger and their public scandals."

"A gap between what the presidency itself has been, and what it has lately and sadly become," he added, referring back to "giants" of presidents and mentioning Democrats Harry Truman and John Kennedy and Republicans Gerald Ford and Dwight Eisenhower.

Dole's litany of alleged wrongdoings included investigations by four independent counsels of Cabinet members and "more than 30 Clinton officials investigated, fired, or forced to resign due to ethical improprieties."

He mentioned the collection of confidential FBI files of Republicans by "a former bar bouncer" working for the White House, the so-called Travelgate firing of longtime White House employees in the travel office and use of Marine helicopters for a staff golf outing.

"And now we see new charges that this administration has allowed a wealthy Indonesian family to buy presidential access, and play a role in foreign policy, in exchange for contributions to the Democratic National Committee," Dole said.
Mindful that an assault on Clinton personally could backfire, Dole said he has never questioned anyone's character and would not now.

"But there is a difference between private character and public ethics, because public ethics is a public trust," Dole said. "When it is violated, the damage is done to our nation, our institutions and our idealism."
The problems of the Clinton administration, Dole said, have become a pattern, "a habit of half-truths, an atmosphere of evasion."
Hammering his theme, Dole contended, "The goal is always to conceal ethical failure, not confront it. We hear, not apologies, but alibis. The buck stops nowhere."
He added, "Sometimes this seems like an epidemic in America. No one will take responsibility for their actions."
A major plank in Dole's campaign has been claims that he can be trusted to keep his word while Clinton does not keep his promises.

He said that promises Clinton made "have little or no relation to his conduct in office. And everything we have learned tells us that four more years of Bill Clinton will mean four more years of discarded pledges and shaded truths."
Dole said, "There is a straight line from indifference to ethical standards in the executive branch to these kind of misleading statements in a campaign."

"Every pledge is subject to endless revision and constant appeal," said Dole. "Every principle is reduced to a tactic, to be changed as circumstances require. Every promise is a posture, temporary and flexible."
If the polls are to believed, Dole said, people will vote for Clinton "even though they believe he is unethical."
Dole challenged the voters to reconsider. "A president who has betrayed your trust has not won your vote," he said. "It is that simple."
